premises: A temperature-induced transition from screw to edge dislocation dominance occurs in BCC refractory HEAs.
This transition leads to a yield strength plateau at high temperatures.
The transition is driven by thermal activation of edge dislocations (e.g., via super-jogging).
The specific alloy NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 exhibits this behavior between 673 K and 1073 K.
In situ neutron diffraction and TEM can distinguish screw vs. edge dislocation populations.
